items.claim: The petuchah recorded on MT 11:1 is presented as corroboration of this unit's onset at MT 11:1, but a paragraph mark is recorded on the verse it follows, so that mark stands after 11:1 and divides 11:1 from 11:2. It is internal to the span 11:1-13, not front-seam evidence. The onset at MT 11:1 has no preceding paragraph mark of any kind: MT 10:22 carries none, and the nearest earlier mark in the witness is the setumah after MT 9:11, twenty-three verses back. The row's own evidence list treats the petuchah after MT 11:6 as internal while treating the one after MT 11:1 as opening the row, though both stand inside the same span. The consequence is that describing MT 11:1 and MT 11:13 together as double-sided paragraph corroboration overstates the record: only the close at MT 11:13 is mark-corroborated.
items.both_sides: Behind the onset: MT 10:22 ends the wheels-and-faces description with no paragraph mark, so nothing in the Masoretic layer marks a division between MT 10:22 and MT 11:1; the nearest earlier mark is the setumah after MT 9:11. Ahead of the onset: the petuchah after MT 11:1 does mark a real division, but between 11:1 and 11:2, where the transport verse gives way to the address to the prophet about the city's schemers. The close is the strong side: a petuchah stands after MT 11:13, and the next unit carries a strict-form word-event onset at MT 11:14. The span therefore holds together on formula and narrative grounds and the medium confidence survives, but the internal division after MT 11:1 is left unaccounted for while the onset is credited with corroboration it does not have.

suggested_fix.fact: the petuchah recorded on MT 11:1 falls after that verse and divides it from MT 11:2, so it is an internal division inside the span rather than onset corroboration; the onset at MT 11:1 carries no preceding paragraph mark, MT 10:22 being unmarked and the nearest earlier mark the setumah after MT 9:11

items.claim: Every Masoretic fact this row asserts holds on the witness. MT 11:14 carries the strict-form word-event onset and is a member of the 39-verse strict set; a petuchah stands after MT 11:13, correctly credited as the mark behind this unit's opening; MT 11:21 closes with the utterance signature and is a member of the 81-verse set. The two setumot inside the span, after MT 11:15 and after MT 11:16, are both disclosed and are the only marks the span contains, so the mark disclosure is complete in both directions. The span holds neither a ketiv/qere site nor a paseq occurrence, and that denial is true on the record.
items.both_sides: Behind the onset a petuchah stands after MT 11:13 and the preceding unit closes on the prophet's cry; at the onset MT 11:14 carries the strict word-event form, and the addressee moves from the men at the gate to the scattered exiles. The close at MT 11:21 carries the utterance signature, and the vision frame resumes only afterwards, at MT 11:22. Both sides are formula-marked, which is why the embedded oracle stands as its own unit inside the still-open vision.

suggested_fix.fact: no change required; the onset, the close and the two internal marks are all true on the witness and the mark disclosure is complete in both directions

items.claim: The parent-seam reading is sound on the witness. MT 11:22 resumes the cherubim-and-wheels vocabulary last carried at MT 10:19, and the splices at MT 11:22 and MT 11:25 collate byte-for-byte as whole verses. A petuchah stands after MT 11:25 and is the only mark inside the span. The row claims no paragraph mark behind its onset at MT 11:22, which is correct, since MT 11:21 carries none. The statement that the span holds neither a ketiv/qere note nor a paseq occurrence is true. The onward contrast is also true: MT 12:1 carries a bare strict-form word-event onset with none of the vision devices.
items.both_sides: On the closing side, the return transport is stated at MT 11:24 and the report to the exiles at MT 11:25, with a petuchah after MT 11:25. On the opening side of the following unit, MT 12:1 carries the strict word-event form and no transport, no glory and no cherubim vocabulary, so the device contrast across the seam is total. That the onset of this row at MT 11:22 has no mark behind it is stated rather than papered over, which is the right handling, since a missing mark is not counter-evidence.

suggested_fix.fact: no change required; the resumption at MT 11:22, the mark after MT 11:25 and the device contrast at MT 12:1 are all true on the witness

items.claim: Two Masoretic-layer statements in this row are not right on the record. First, the row states that the Qere-adaptation editorial note class is confined to MT 14:14 and MT 14:20. That note stands on three verses book-wide: MT 14:14, MT 14:20 and MT 28:3. The exclusivity is therefore false, although the point it serves is true, since neither of the two notes inside this span belongs to that class. Second, the row prints a read form for the ketiv/qere site at MT 12:14 under an original-language reference, and that string occurs nowhere in the witness text of the book. The written form the row gives at that site does occur there, as unvocalized consonants; the read form is carried only by the variant apparatus. The substantive disclosures are otherwise correct: MT 12:14 is the only ketiv/qere site in MT chapters 11 and 12, and the two editorial notes inside the span, at MT 12:10 on a vowel reading and MT 12:12 on an accent reading, are both accurately characterised.
items.both_sides: On the seam question the row is sound on both sides: MT 12:8 carries a word-event onset with an infixed temporal phrase, one of exactly two such verses book-wide, and behind it a petuchah stands after MT 12:7; the close at MT 12:15 and MT 12:16 carries the recognition refrain twice, both verses being members of the 28-verse strict set, with a petuchah after MT 12:16. Neither challenged statement bears on where the boundaries sit, so the span and its confidence are untouched; both are disclosure-accuracy defects inside the evidence and device fields. The read-form point matters because a reader of this row alone cannot tell that the printed form is apparatus-only rather than witness text.

suggested_fix.fact: the Qere-adaptation editorial note stands on three verses book-wide, MT 14:14, MT 14:20 and MT 28:3, so that class is not confined to the first two; and at the ketiv/qere site the read form is carried only by the variant apparatus, the running witness text showing the unvocalized written consonants at that point, so the site is better named than the read form rendered as an original-language quotation

items.claim: The row's separation of the two recognition counts is correct and is the point worth affirming. MT 12:17 carries the strict-form word-event onset and is a member of the 39-verse strict set; a petuchah stands after MT 12:16 behind that onset, and another after MT 12:20 at the close, the latter being the only mark inside the span. MT 12:20 closes with the second-person-plural recognition wording, and the figure of twenty-one verses book-wide for that family re-derives exactly from the witness consonants, the resulting verse list matching the ruled list member for member with MT 12:20 among them. MT 12:20 is correctly excluded from the 28-verse strict set, and it also falls outside the five-verse second-person-singular variant, so declining to blend the counts is right. The span holds neither a ketiv/qere site nor a paseq occurrence, and that denial is true.
items.both_sides: Behind the onset a petuchah stands after MT 12:16 and the preceding unit has closed on its doubled refrain. At the close a petuchah stands after MT 12:20, and the following unit carries a strict-form word-event onset at MT 12:21. Both sides of this four-verse unit are marked, which is why a unit this short is nonetheless well founded.

suggested_fix.fact: no change required; the twenty-one-verse figure for the second-person-plural recognition family re-derives byte-exactly and MT 12:20 belongs to that family rather than to the strict set

items.claim: Every Masoretic claim holds. Both sides are marked and formula-bounded, so the quoted proverb and its refutation stand as one unbroken unit with no internal formula seam, as the row says.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: Whether the internal paragraph division after MT 11:1 should be read as arguing a competing seam at MT 11:2, splitting the transport verse from the address about the city's schemers.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: I judged it internal texture and kept the span whole, because MT 11:2 carries no word-event onset and the addressee is continuous, and because a paragraph mark informs a boundary without deciding one alone. A reviewer weighting the Masoretic layer more heavily could reach a different answer, and the row currently discusses MT 11:5 as its sub-onset without surfacing this division at all.

It is probably better settled once by a normalizer rule than by rewording single rows, which is why I did not raise it to a challenge of its own.
